clue.text: A healthy exercise, in accordance with principles of state

definitions.text: in accordance with principles of state

blocks.note: first meaning: a walk taken for the sake of one's health

blocks.clueFragment: in accordance with principles of state
blocks.note: second meaning: conforming to a country's founding law

explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits two unrelated senses of one long word: a noun for a brisk walk and an adjective from political law.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle walk for health is an old-fashioned noun sense; the adjective describes anything permitted by a nation's founding charter.

clue.text: Tory PM's main cut upset his extreme opponents

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A Conservative prime minister's headline budget cut angers the far left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' points back to the Tory in the surface: the far-left party is the Conservatives' most extreme political opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marxist political organisation sits at the opposite end of the spectrum from Conservatives, making it their most radical adversary.

clue.text: Obtains inside information set up for savings

indicators.note: one word goes inside another, so the verb for obtaining sits within the word for information
in a down entry, setting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: to obtain is to get
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone acts on insider knowledge to build up a financial cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, short for general information; in a down clue 'set up' reads the result from the bottom upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money put aside for the future, so it names a person's savings.

clue.text: He orchestrates tributes to rebuilt team's star

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone organises praise for the leading player of a team that has been reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tributes' is part of the definition, not wordplay: a toast is a tribute, and this person calls for them at a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: At a banquet the official who announces the speakers and proposes each raised glass in honour of someone is directing the tributes.

clue.text: Part of suite, traditionally for quartet

indicators.note: the answer is only a portion of the following words, sitting inside them

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A musical suite is customarily written for four instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'quartet' look like a string group, but it simply means a set of four.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a group or set of four things, from the Greek for four, just as a quartet is.

clue.text: Piece of music I put in frantic tempo

indicators.note: frantic means wild and disordered, so the letters of the word it describes are jumbled
placing one thing in another means the number goes inside the scrambled word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral I is the number one
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician confesses to playing a piece at a frenzied speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not the speaker but the numeral one, spelt out and placed after the first letter of the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone poem is an orchestral composition in one movement illustrating a story or scene, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: Public mouthpiece?

indicators.note: a piece is only a fragment, so the answer is a portion taken from the word before it

blocks.note: the middle three letters of the word mouth, read as a piece of that word

explanation.surface: A spokesperson for the people, the question mark hints that it is not what it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouthpiece' looks like one word meaning spokesperson, but it splits into the source word and an indicator for a piece of it.
explanation.definitionFit: When a secret is out it has become publicly known, so the adjective can stand for public.

clue.text: Opposed to increases in a budget, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows
one item goes in the others, so the word for increases sits between the single letters

blocks.note: taken as written
increases are gains
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone objects to the rises in spending in a budget.
explanation.walkthrough: GAINS sits inside A and T, the last letter of budget.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to be opposed to it; both phrases take an object after them.

clue.text: Poet composed a friendly sonnet I rejected

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged into something new
a letter that is rejected is thrown out, so it is removed from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written
this letter is the one removed

explanation.surface: A poet wrote a warm sonnet, but the speaker turned it down.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from the phrase, then rearrange the remaining fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate who wrote The Charge of the Light Brigade and In Memoriam.

clue.text: Male is discarded, in part inappropriately

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for male
taken as written
something cast off has been thrown away

explanation.surface: A man is dropped, partly because he was unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' sounds like 'partly', but it means in a theatrical role: an actor given the wrong role is this.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor placed in a role that does not suit them has been given the part unsuitably, which is exactly what the word describes.

clue.text: Clear everyone over time in court action

blocks.note: to clear is to net, as with a profit after costs
the setter's letter here is hard to source; no common abbreviation gives it from these words
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A judge orders the room emptied of everyone after the hearing overruns.
explanation.walkthrough: NET and ALL are clear, but the B between them has no standard source in 'over time'; the clue as printed does not fully account for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game played on a hard court, so a match of it is action on a court.

clue.text: Application for employment

blocks.note: first meaning: the act of putting something to work
second meaning: the act of using something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a job application, but both words are nouns for putting a thing into service.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the act of putting something into service, which both application and employment also mean.

clue.text: Bouncy performer coach includes mainly plays on left, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept
one word including others holds them inside it

blocks.note: a coach trains athletes
first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An energetic coach mostly fields his side on the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a vehicle or the subject of the sentence, but it is the container word; 'initially' applies to all four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who performs on a trampoline springs up and down, so they are literally a bouncy performer.

clue.text: Trickery from cricket side remained out of order

indicators.note: letters out of order are no longer in their proper sequence, so they get rearranged

blocks.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the side behind the batsman's legs
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheating cricket team stayed in a disorderly state.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Legerdemain is sleight of hand, so it means conjuring trickery or deception.

clue.text: Dressed and ready for drive

blocks.note: first meaning: wearing one's gear or kit
second meaning: a car with a gear engaged is set to move

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone dressed for a drive; the phrase is read once as wearing clothes and once as a car's gearbox engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is both clothing and the transmission setting of a car, so the phrase means clothed or set to move off.

clue.text: Bearing a load we had crew put inside

indicators.note: something put inside another goes into its middle, so the crew word sits within the contraction

blocks.note: we had is contracted to we'd, written without the apostrophe
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A captain recalls that the crew was loaded on board their vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We had' must be contracted with its apostrophe dropped; a rowing crew in a racing boat is called an eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighted carries extra weight, so it is bearing a load.

clue.text: Places of refuge in castle I'd destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone sheltering in a castle confesses they wrecked it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a ruined castle, which matches the fortress meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Citadels are fortresses guarding a city, where people retreat for safety, so they are places of refuge.

clue.text: Run away from dog after attack

blocks.note: a turn is a sudden bout or attack of illness
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a dog after it has gone for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you to place the dog word after the attack word; 'attack' is a turn, as in a dizzy turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom for fleeing, turning so that only one's back is seen, so it means run away.

clue.text: Somewhat disreputable service attached to school

blocks.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of Britain's armed services
a school is a group of fish, so fish stand for the school

explanation.surface: A slightly shady military man has been posted to a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is not a place of learning but a shoal, and FISH stands in for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffish person is unconventional in a slightly louche, rakish way, which is to say somewhat disreputable.

clue.text: Position for captain in game

blocks.note: first meaning: the raised platform from which a ship is commanded
second meaning: the card game for two pairs of partners

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team captain's place on a sports field; in fact one sense is nautical and the other is cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain stands on the command deck known by this name, and the word also names the trick-taking card game.

clue.text: Don't accept reduction

blocks.note: first meaning: to turn down an offer, a verb
second meaning: a fall or lessening, a noun

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as refusing a price cut, but the word is first a verb for refusing and then a noun for falling off.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to refuse politely, and a decline is a gradual decrease, so the word fills both roles.

clue.text: Watch over writing, say, for old poet

indicators.note: one thing spread over another covers it, so the watch word wraps around the letter

blocks.note: a vigil is a watch kept through the night
writing is one of the three Rs, so R can represent it; 'say' flags the example

explanation.surface: A guard keeps watch over someone's manuscript to protect an ancient poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so R stands for writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil was the Roman poet who wrote the Aeneid, so he is an ancient poet.

clue.text: Female in a company with musical backing? That's right

indicators.note: one letter placed in the following words sits inside them
something backing runs in the opposite direction, so the musical's name is read from end to start

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a firm is a company
Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: A woman joins a firm that is putting money behind a stage show and asks if that's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical backing' looks like accompaniment, but it asks for a named stage show written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An affirmative answer is a yes, so the word says that's right, as in radio talk.

clue.text: Preserve word Americans, Canadians, and Mexicans have in common

indicators.note: what several words have in common is a string sitting inside each of them

blocks.note: the same three-letter string appears inside each of these three nationality words

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a word shared by the three North American peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a riddle about North America, but the shared word is literally three letters found in each nationality's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To can food is to seal it in a tin to keep it, so it means to preserve.

clue.text: Limited flow in river accommodated by fish, in a way

indicators.note: something accommodated by another is housed inside it

blocks.note: tickling trout is an old way of catching fish by hand
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A sparse stream of water in a river is used by someone fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickling is a poacher's method of catching trout by stroking them underwater until they can be flipped out, which is why 'in a way' qualifies 'fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle is a thin, slow stream of liquid, so it is a limited flow.

clue.text: Not altogether cordial relations

indicators.note: not altogether means not the whole thing, so the end of the word is cut away

blocks.note: cordial means warm and kind

explanation.surface: Family members who are not entirely warm towards each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of KIND is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Kin are one's family, the people one is related to, so the word means relations.

clue.text: Handlers of football teams answer with whoppers after game

indicators.note: after tells the solver that the following pieces come behind the game word in the answer

blocks.note: Go is the Japanese board game
A is the standard abbreviation for answer
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: Football managers tell tall tales after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handlers' suggests managers, but it means the only players in a football team allowed to handle the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Goalkeepers are the one player per side permitted to touch the ball with their hands, so they are its handlers.

clue.text: With which some Asians cover bulb for garden plant

definitions.text: With which some Asians cover bulb

blocks.clueFragment: With which some Asians cover bulb
blocks.note: first meaning: a collapsible paper shade placed around a light, associated with China
second meaning: the physalis, whose orange seed cases resemble paper shades

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' tempts a gardening reading alongside 'garden plant', but here it is a light bulb inside a paper shade.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper lamp shade is traditional in China, and the physalis plant is named after it for its papery orange husks.
